question: Gangubai Hangal belonged to the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gangubai Hangal (1913-2009) was a legendary Hindustani classical vocalist belonging to the Kirana gharana, trained under Sawai Gandharva. (गंगूबाई हंगल — किराना घराना)

 

• The Kirana gharana was founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan and is known for its emphasis on swara (note) purity and slow, meditative raga elaboration (bol-alap).

 

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1971) and Padma Vibhushan (2002) for her contribution to Hindustani classical music, and was known for her deep, resonant voice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other prominent Kirana gharana vocalists include Bhimsen Joshi and Prabha Atre, also disciples in the same lineage.

 

NOTE

 

• Gwalior gharana (Option 1): The oldest khyal gharana, associated with Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar.

 

• Banaras gharana (Option 3): Known for its distinct thumri and tappa tradition.

 

• Agra gharana (Option 4): Founded by Ustad Ghagge Khuda Baksh, known for its forceful nom-tom alap style.

question: Which of the following districts of India is an example of an industrial district?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kota.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kota, in Rajasthan, is cited as an example of an industrial district, known for its cluster of chemical, fertiliser and thermal-power industries. (कोटा — औद्योगिक जिला)

 

• Major industrial units located in and around Kota include Chambal Fertilisers and Chemicals Limited and the Kota Super Thermal Power Station, along with several chemical and engineering units, making it one of Rajasthan's leading industrial centres.

 

• Kota is situated on the banks of the Chambal River; while it is also nationally known as a hub for competitive-exam coaching institutes, it is its industrial base that makes it an example of an industrial district.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable industrial districts/regions of India include Ludhiana (hosiery), Coimbatore (textiles/engineering) and Vadodara (petrochemicals).

 

NOTE

 

• Faridabad (Option 1): An industrial town of Haryana in the NCR, but not the district cited as this specific example.

 

• Meerut (Option 2): Known chiefly for sports-goods and scissors manufacturing, not classified here as an industrial district.

 

• Jaipur (Option 4): Known as the Pink City, primarily an administrative, tourism and handicrafts centre rather than a heavy-industry district.

question: Which among the following is NOT a classification criterion of drugs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Behavioural condition.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Drugs are classified on the basis of pharmacological effect, chemical structure, and molecular target (drug action) — "behavioural condition" is not one of the standard classification criteria. (औषध वर्गीकरण — व्यवहारिक स्थिति मापदंड नहीं है)

 

• Classification by pharmacological effect groups drugs by the effect they produce — e.g., analgesics relieve pain.

 

• Classification by chemical structure groups drugs that share a common core structure and often show similar pharmacological activity, e.g., sulphonamides.

 

• Classification by molecular targets is considered most useful for medicinal chemists — it groups drugs based on the specific biomolecule (usually an enzyme or receptor) they act upon.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Drugs may also be classified on the basis of the specific biochemical process/pathway they act on within the body.

 

NOTE

 

• Chemical structure (Option 1): A recognised classification criterion — structurally similar drugs often show similar effects.

 

• Molecular target (Option 2): A recognised, clinically important classification criterion, e.g., drugs targeting a particular enzyme or receptor.

 

• Pharmacological effect (Option 4): A recognised classification criterion, e.g., classifying drugs as analgesics or antiseptics.

question: The Non-Cooperation Movement was called off after which of the following incidents?
option_1: Outbreak of the First World War
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chauri-Chaura incident.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22), launched by Mahatma Gandhi, was called off after the Chauri-Chaura incident of 5 February 1922. (चौरी चौरा कांड — असहयोग आंदोलन वापस)

 

• At Chauri Chaura, a village in the Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh, an angry mob set fire to a police station, killing about 22-23 policemen, after police fired on a peaceful procession.

 

• Believing the movement had turned violent and deviated from the principle of non-violence (ahimsa), Gandhi unilaterally withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement on 12 February 1922.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched partly in response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919) and the Khilafat issue, and was formally adopted at the Calcutta Special Session of the Congress (1920).

 

NOTE

 

• Outbreak of the First World War (Option 1): Occurred in 1914, well before the Non-Cooperation Movement began.

 

• Kakori train robbery (Option 2): Took place in 1925, an action by revolutionaries of the HRA, unrelated to this movement's withdrawal.

 

• Komagata Maru incident (Option 4): Occurred in 1914, involving Indian emigrants denied entry into Canada, unrelated to the movement's withdrawal.

question:
With reference to Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, consider the following statements.

a) He protested child marriage and polygamy.

b) Due to his efforts, the first Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856, was introduced.

c) He was primarily known for his scholarship in Persian language.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is a, b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement (a) is correct: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a strong social reformer who protested against child marriage and Kulin polygamy, and championed women's education. (ईश्वर चंद्र विद्यासागर — विधवा पुनर्विवाह)

 

• Statement (b) is correct: Due to his relentless efforts and petitions, the Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856 was enacted, legalising the remarriage of Hindu widows.

 

• Statement (c) is incorrect: Vidyasagar was primarily a scholar of Sanskrit — he was titled "Vidyasagar" (ocean of learning) for his Sanskrit scholarship, not for Persian.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Vidyasagar reformed the Sanskrit College curriculum, opposed child marriage and Kulin polygamy, and helped establish several schools promoting girls' education in Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• a, b, c (Option 1): Incorrect because statement (c) is factually wrong.

 

• a, c (Option 3): Incorrect because statement (c) is factually wrong, even though (a) is correct.

 

• b, c (Option 4): Incorrect because statement (c) is factually wrong, even though (b) is correct.

question: What happens when two forces act in the opposite directions on an object?
option_1: The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two objects.
option_2: The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two forces.
option_3: The net force acting on the object is the total of the two forces.
option_4: The net force acting on the object is the sum of the two objects.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The net force acting on the object is the difference between the two forces.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When two forces act on an object in opposite directions, the net (resultant) force is the difference between the magnitudes of the two forces, acting in the direction of the larger force. (विपरीत दिशा में बल — बलों का अंतर)

 

• This follows from the vector nature of force: forces acting along the same line but in opposite senses partially cancel each other out.

 

• In contrast, when two forces act in the same direction, the net force is the sum of the two forces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Force is a vector quantity, measured in newtons (N); the net force determines the resulting acceleration of an object as per F = ma (Newton's second law).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Incorrectly refers to "the difference between the two objects" instead of forces.

 

• Option 3: Incorrect; the total (sum) of the two forces applies only when they act in the same direction, not opposite directions.

 

• Option 4: Incorrectly refers to "the sum of the two objects", which is meaningless since objects are not summed.

question: Which industrial policy marked the beginning of liberalisation in the Indian industry, reducing the restrictions on private companies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Industrial Policy 1991.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The New Industrial Policy of 1991, introduced under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh, marked the beginning of Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation (LPG) reforms in India. (औद्योगिक नीति 1991 — उदारीकरण)

 

• It drastically reduced the number of industries reserved for the public sector, abolished industrial licensing (License Raj) for most industries, and removed restrictions under the MRTP Act on large business houses.

 

• It also encouraged Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and foreign technology agreements, opening the Indian economy to global competition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 1991 reforms were triggered by a severe Balance of Payments crisis, which forced India to pledge gold reserves and approach the IMF for a loan.

 

NOTE

 

• Industrial Policy 1980 (Option 2): Focused on promoting effective utilisation of licensed capacity and revival of sick industrial units.

 

• Industrial Policy 1977 (Option 3): Emphasised the promotion of small-scale and cottage industries.

 

• Industrial Policy 1956 (Option 4): Laid the framework for a socialistic pattern of society, dividing industries into public, private and joint sectors (Schedules A, B, C).

question: The first Indian woman to hold the Under-20 World Wrestling Championship is _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Antim Panghal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Antim Panghal became the first Indian woman to win a gold medal at the U20 World Wrestling Championships, in the 53 kg freestyle category in 2022, at the age of 17. (अंतिम पंघाल — प्रथम भारतीय महिला अंडर-20 विश्व चैंपियन)

 

• She hails from Hisar, Haryana, a region known for producing several top Indian wrestlers.

 

• She went on to defend her U20 world title in 2023, further cementing her reputation as one of India's leading young wrestling talents, and later represented India at senior international events including the Asian Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other prominent Indian women wrestlers include Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik (India's first female Olympic wrestling medallist, Rio 2016) and Sarita Mor.

 

NOTE

 

• Pranati Nayak (Option 2): An Indian gymnast, not a wrestler.

 

• Swati Sanjay (Option 3) and Hina Khalifa (Option 4): Not associated with winning the U20 World Wrestling Championship title for India.

question: The name of the strait between the Pacific and Arctic oceans, separating the Chukchi Peninsula of the Russian Far East from the Seward Peninsula of Alaska, is the:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bering Strait.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Bering Strait connects the Pacific Ocean (Bering Sea) with the Arctic Ocean (Chukchi Sea), separating the Chukchi Peninsula of Russia from the Seward Peninsula of Alaska, USA. (बेरिंग जलडमरूमध्य — रूस और अलास्का)

 

• It is named after the Danish-Russian navigator Vitus Bering, who explored the region in the 18th century.

 

• At its narrowest point, the strait is only about 82 km (51 miles) wide, and the Diomede Islands (one belonging to the USA, the other to Russia) lie within it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• During the last Ice Age, a land bridge called Beringia existed here, believed to be the route by which early humans migrated from Asia into the Americas.

 

NOTE

 

• Davis Strait (Option 1): Located between Greenland and Baffin Island (Canada), connecting the Atlantic Ocean and Baffin Bay.

 

• Florida Strait (Option 2): Located between Florida (USA) and Cuba, connecting the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean.

 

• Messina Strait (Option 4): Located between the Italian mainland and the island of Sicily.

question: Which Committee identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Justice Verma Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Justice J.S. Verma Committee (1999), constituted by the Ministry of Human Resource Development, was tasked with operationalising the teaching of Fundamental Duties in educational institutions. (जस्टिस वर्मा समिति — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• The committee identified that legal provisions already existed for the implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A, even though the article itself is non-justiciable.

 

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and appear in Part IVA (Article 51A).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Originally there were 10 Fundamental Duties; an 11th ("to provide opportunities for education to children between 6-14 years") was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

NOTE

 

• Justice Mulla Committee (Option 1): The Mulla Committee dealt with jail/prison reforms, not Fundamental Duties.

 

• Justice Sapre Committee (Option 3): Not associated with the implementation of Fundamental Duties.

 

• Justice VR Krishna Iyer Committee (Option 4): Known for its work on prison reforms and the status of women, not specifically Fundamental Duties.

question: ‘Ungalil Oruvan’ (One Among You) is the autobiography of which of the following chief ministers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is MK Stalin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Ungalil Oruvan' (One Among You) is the autobiography of M.K. Stalin, the current Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu and leader of the DMK. (उंगलिल ओरुवन — एम.के. स्टालिन)

 

• The book traces his political journey — from his early days in student politics and the DMK movement, through the Emergency period, to his rise as a senior party leader.

 

• M.K. Stalin is the son of former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi, and became Chief Minister in May 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tamil Nadu's Dravidian movement has a strong tradition of leader-writers, including C.N. Annadurai and M. Karunanidhi.

 

NOTE

 

• K Chandrashekhar Rao (Option 2): Former Chief Minister of Telangana, founder of the BRS (formerly TRS).

 

• Basavaraj Bommai (Option 3): Former Chief Minister of Karnataka.

 

• Pinarayi Vijayan (Option 4): Chief Minister of Kerala, leader of the CPI(M).

question: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution deals with the parliament and it's proceedings?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 79 to 122.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Articles 79 to 122, in Part V, Chapter II of the Indian Constitution, deal with "The Union Parliament" — its composition, powers, procedures and privileges. (अनुच्छेद 79-122 — संसद)

 

• Article 79 establishes the Parliament, consisting of the President, the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People).

 

• This range covers provisions such as qualification of members (Art. 84), sessions of Parliament (Art. 85), legislative procedure (Arts. 107-111), and the Budget/Money Bills (Arts. 110, 112).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 368 deals with the procedure for constitutional amendment, while Articles 245-255 deal with legislative relations between the Union and the states.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 51A (Option 1): Lists the Fundamental Duties of citizens.

 

• Article 36 to 51 (Option 2): Contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV).

 

• Article 12 to 35 (Option 4): Contains the Fundamental Rights (Part III).

question: What was India's annual exponential growth rate as per the 2011 Census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.64%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census of India, the population grew from 102.87 crore (2001) to 121.09 crore (2011), a decadal growth rate of 17.64%, corresponding to an annual exponential growth rate of 1.64%. (2011 जनगणना — वार्षिक चरघातांकी वृद्धि दर 1.64%)

 

• This was a decline from the 1991-2001 decade's exponential growth rate of 1.97%, reflecting a gradually slowing pace of population growth.

 

• Uttar Pradesh remained India's most populous state in 2011, while some north-eastern and central states recorded comparatively higher growth rates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India (7th since independence), with the slogan "Our Census, Our Future"; India's sex ratio in 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males.

 

NOTE

 

• 1.10% (Option 1), 4.34% (Option 3), 3.54% (Option 4): None of these correspond to India's actual 2001-2011 annual exponential growth rate recorded by the Census, which is 1.64%.

question: The Kuchipudi dance belongs to which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kuchipudi is a classical dance form that originated in the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh (Krishna district). (कुचिपुड़ी — आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• It developed as a dance-drama performed by Brahmin men (Bhagavatulu) in temples, based on stories from Hindu texts, and is traditionally attributed to the 17th-century saint Siddhendra Yogi.

 

• A distinctive feature of Kuchipudi is the Tarangam item, in which the dancer performs while standing on the rim of a brass plate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other classical dance forms include Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Odissi (Odisha), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 1): Home to Bharatanatyam, not Kuchipudi.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Not the state of origin of any of the classical dance forms of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

• Manipur (Option 4): Home to Manipuri classical dance.

question: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C3H8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• C3H8 (propane) is a saturated hydrocarbon (alkane), containing only single covalent bonds between carbon atoms, following the general formula CnH2n+2. (संतृप्त हाइड्रोकार्बन — C3H8)

 

• Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) are hydrocarbons in which every carbon atom is bonded to the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms.

 

• Unsaturated hydrocarbons, in contrast, contain at least one double bond (alkenes, CnH2n) or triple bond (alkynes, CnH2n-2) between carbon atoms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of alkanes include methane (CH4), ethane (C2H6) and butane (C4H10).

 

NOTE

 

• C6H6 (Option 2): Benzene, an aromatic unsaturated hydrocarbon with alternating double bonds.

 

• C2H4 (Option 3): Ethylene (ethene), an unsaturated alkene with one C=C double bond.

 

• C4H8 (Option 4): Butene, an unsaturated alkene with one C=C double bond.

question: The final match of IPL 2023 was hosted by which of the following cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The final of IPL 2023 (16th season) was held at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, on 29-30 May 2023 (decided on the reserve day due to rain). (आईपीएल 2023 फाइनल — अहमदाबाद)

 

• Chennai Super Kings (CSK), captained by MS Dhoni, defeated Gujarat Titans (GT) in the final to win their 5th IPL title, equalling Mumbai Indians' record.

 

• The match was played at the world's largest cricket stadium, in front of a record crowd.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gujarat Titans, led by Hardik Pandya, had won the IPL 2022 title in their debut season.

 

NOTE

 

• Bengaluru (Option 1), Chennai (Option 2), Mumbai (Option 3): These cities hosted other IPL 2023 league/qualifier matches but not the final, which was held at Ahmedabad.

question: Which of the following Rajiv Gandhi National Sadbhavana Awards was conferred on Ustad Amjad Ali Khan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21st.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 21st Rajiv Gandhi National Sadbhavana Award was conferred on the eminent sarod maestro Ustad Amjad Ali Khan in April 2014, in recognition of his contribution to promoting communal harmony and national integration through music. (राजीव गांधी राष्ट्रीय सद्भावना पुरस्कार — उस्ताद अमजद अली खान)

 

• The Rajiv Gandhi National Sadbhavana Award is conferred annually by the All India Congress Committee (AICC) in memory of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, for promoting communal harmony and peace.

 

• Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a renowned sarod player of the Senia Bangash gharana, and has also received the Padma Vibhushan and other high civilian honours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The award was instituted in 1992, and its past recipients include eminent personalities from diverse fields who have worked to promote communal harmony.

 

NOTE

 

• 20th, 19th, 18th (Options 1, 2, 4): These editions of the award were conferred on other recipients in different years, not on Ustad Amjad Ali Khan.

question: A large number of words are derived from the word ‘Go’ meaning cow. A wealthy person was known as ________ in Vedic times.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gomat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Vedic times, many words were derived from 'go', meaning cow; a wealthy person (one possessing many cows) was known as 'gomat'. (गोमत — वैदिक काल में धनी व्यक्ति)

 

• Other such derived words include 'duhitr' (daughter, literally "one who milks the cow") and 'gaveshana' (literally "search for cows", which came to mean "battle/war").

 

• This reflects the centrality of cattle wealth (pashudhan) in the pastoral-agrarian economy of the Rigvedic period, where cattle served as a measure of wealth and were often the cause of conflict between tribes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term 'gopa'/'gopala' (protector of cows) was also used for a king/chief, again reflecting the importance of cattle in Vedic society.

 

NOTE

 

• Gotra (Option 2): Refers to lineage/clan descent, not wealth.

 

• Gabaksha (Option 3): Literally "cow's eye", a term used for a type of ornamental window/arch in later architecture, not a wealthy person.

 

• Gaveshana (Option 4): Literally "search for cows", which evolved to mean "battle" or "war", not wealth.

question: In which state of India is the Chandra Prabha Wildlife Sanctuary located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chandra Prabha Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Chandauli district of Uttar Pradesh, about 70 km from Varanasi. (चंद्रप्रभा वन्यजीव अभयारण्य — उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• It was established in 1957 and is notable for an early, unsuccessful attempt to reintroduce Asiatic lions from Gir (Gujarat) in 1958.

 

• The sanctuary features the Chandraprabha and Naugarh rivers and waterfalls, and forms part of a larger forest corridor connecting to Madhya Pradesh and Bihar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important wildlife sanctuaries/parks of Uttar Pradesh include Katarniaghat Wildlife Sanctuary, Dudhwa National Park and Kaimoor Wildlife Sanctuary.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1), Gujarat (Option 2), Madhya Pradesh (Option 4): These states have their own well-known sanctuaries, but the Chandra Prabha Wildlife Sanctuary specifically is located in Uttar Pradesh.

question: Which of the following is a correct statement?
option_1: National Income is GNP at FC.
option_2: National Income is NDP at MP.
option_3: National Income is GDP at MP.
option_4: National Income is NNP at FC.
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Income is NNP at FC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In economics, National Income is conventionally defined as Net National Product at Factor Cost (NNP at FC) — the total factor income earned by normal residents of a country during a year. (राष्ट्रीय आय — NNP एट FC)

 

• NNP at FC = GNP at Market Price − Depreciation − Net Indirect Taxes (Indirect Taxes − Subsidies), i.e., it is the sum of wages, rent, interest and profit earned by all factors of production.

 

• This measure excludes depreciation (capital consumption) and adjusts market prices to factor cost by removing the effect of indirect taxes and subsidies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• GDP (Gross Domestic Product) measures output within a country's domestic territory, while GNP adds net factor income from abroad to GDP.

 

NOTE

 

• National Income is GNP at FC (Option 1): Incorrect; GNP at FC still includes depreciation, whereas National Income is a *net* concept.

 

• National Income is NDP at MP (Option 2): Incorrect; this is a market-price and domestic measure, not a factor-cost, national measure.

 

• National Income is GDP at MP (Option 3): Incorrect; this is a gross, domestic, market-price measure — National Income requires net, national, factor-cost.

question: Who among the following famous badminton players won Swiss Open 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PV Sindhu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PV Sindhu won the women's singles title at the Swiss Open 2022 (a BWF Super 300 tournament), defeating Busanan Ongbamrungphan of Thailand in the final. (स्विस ओपन 2022 — पीवी सिंधु)

 

• This was Sindhu's second Swiss Open title, part of a strong run of form in 2022 that also included a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2022.

 

• PV Sindhu is a two-time Olympic medallist (silver at Rio 2016, bronze at Tokyo 2020) and a former World Champion (2019) in badminton.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PV Sindhu hails from Hyderabad, Telangana, and has been honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna and Padma Bhushan.

 

NOTE

 

• Jwala Gutta (Option 1): A former Indian badminton doubles player, not associated with this win.

 

• Aparna Popat (Option 2): A former Indian badminton singles player, now a coach/administrator, not the 2022 Swiss Open winner.

 

• Saina Nehwal (Option 3): A leading Indian badminton player and Olympic medallist, but she did not win the Swiss Open 2022 title.

question: The _________ portal is a platform provided by the Govt. of India for famers to attain any information related to agriculture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Farmer's.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Farmers' Portal is a one-stop platform launched by the Government of India (Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare) to provide farmers information related to seeds, farm machinery, fertilisers, pesticides, crop insurance, soil health, weather and market prices. (फार्मर्स पोर्टल — कृषि जानकारी)

 

• It aims to provide personalised, location-specific and crop-specific information to farmers through a single digital window, as part of the push for digital agriculture.

 

• It complements other agriculture-related e-governance initiatives such as mKisan, Kisan Call Centre and PM-KISAN.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Another key agri-tech government platform is e-NAM (National Agriculture Market), used for online trading of agricultural commodities.

 

NOTE

 

• Cropland, Agricultural, Cultivation (Options 1, 3, 4): These are not the official name of the Government of India's farmer-information portal; the correct, official name is the Farmers' Portal.

question: What is iGOT launched by the Government of India in April 2020?
option_1: Online training portal for COVID-19 management
option_2: Online portal for scholarships to single girl child
option_4: Online portal for social security schemes
solution_text:
The correct answer is Online training portal for COVID-19 management.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• iGOT (Integrated Government Online Training) is an online training platform launched by the Government of India in April 2020, initially to train healthcare and frontline workers in COVID-19 management. (आईगॉट — कोविड-19 प्रशिक्षण पोर्टल)

 

• It was developed by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare with partners such as NIHFW, and hosted on the DIKSHA platform of the Ministry of Education.

 

• The platform was later expanded into iGOT Karmayogi, a broader capacity-building platform for all civil servants under Mission Karmayogi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• iGOT Karmayogi was launched in 2022 as part of the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB).

 

NOTE

 

• Online portal for scholarships to single girl child (Option 2): Refers to schemes offered separately (e.g., CBSE Single Girl Child Scholarship), not iGOT.

 

• Online portal for digital payments (Option 3): Refers to platforms such as BHIM/UPI, not iGOT.

 

• Online portal for social security schemes (Option 4): Refers to platforms such as eShram, not iGOT.

question: The Pratiharas who first had their capital at Bhinmal gained prominence during the rule of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagabhatta I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, which first had its capital at Bhinmal (in present-day Rajasthan), gained prominence under Nagabhatta I in the 8th century CE. (नागभट्ट प्रथम — प्रतिहार वंश)

 

• Nagabhatta I is credited with checking the advance of Arab invaders from Sindh into India in the early 8th century, establishing the Pratiharas as a major regional power.

 

• The Pratiharas later shifted their capital to Kannauj and became one of the three major powers in the "Tripartite Struggle" for control of Kannauj, alongside the Palas and the Rashtrakutas; their greatest ruler was Mihira Bhoja.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pratiharas, also known as the Gurjara-Pratiharas, are credited with resisting Arab incursions into India for a considerable period, earning them the title "Bulwark of India against Arab invasions".

 

NOTE

 

• Nagarjuna (Option 2): A renowned Buddhist philosopher of the Madhyamaka school, unrelated to the Pratiharas.

 

• Devpala (Option 3): A powerful ruler of the Pala dynasty of Bengal, a rival of the Pratiharas in the Tripartite Struggle.

 

• Kanishka (Option 4): A famous ruler of the Kushana dynasty, who ruled several centuries before the Pratiharas.

question: In India, Teachers’ Day is celebrated annually on September 5 to mark the birthday of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Teachers' Day is celebrated in India every year on 5 September to mark the birth anniversary of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, India's first Vice President and second President. (शिक्षक दिवस — डॉ. सर्वपल्ली राधाकृष्णन)

 

• Dr. Radhakrishnan was a distinguished philosopher, scholar and teacher; when his students wished to celebrate his birthday, he asked instead that the day be observed as Teachers' Day, honouring all teachers.

 

• He served as President of India from 1962 to 1967, and earlier as Vice President from 1952 to 1962.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Internationally, World Teachers' Day is observed on 5 October, as designated by UNESCO.

 

NOTE

 

• APJ Abdul Kalam (Option 1): India's 11th President; his birthday (15 October) is observed as World Students' Day.

 

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (Option 2): Known as the "Iron Man of India"; his birthday (31 October) is observed as National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas).

 

• Subash Chandra Bose (Option 4): Freedom fighter; his birthday (23 January) is observed as Parakram Diwas.
